lens: Maintainability and code quality — structure, module boundaries, file sizes, coupling, duplication (memory vs supabase repository parity, the 404-line Repository interface), comment density and accuracy, naming drift, schema.ts, component sizes, what the tests actually prove, whether CLAUDE.md's enforced rules hold, TypeScript strictness.
strengths: The authorisation seams are real seams, and they hold. lib/catalogue-access.ts is 88 lines with a single exhaustive switch (lines 74-87) and 92% line coverage; lib/admin/session.ts is 120 lines and is genuinely the only place org_id enters a query. I walked all 60 API route files: every route under app/api/admin/ (including all 11 platform routes) calls requireOperator, requireOwnedCatalogue, requireEditableCatalogue or requirePlatformAdmin. Zero exceptions. That is unusual at 179 commits and is the single best thing in the repo.

The module system is a textbook plug-in boundary and it is enforced structurally, not by convention. modules/contract.ts (126 lines) defines the interface, modules/registry.ts (117 lines) is the only wiring point, and tests/unit/registry.test.ts:123-157 walks app/, components/ and lib/ on disk and fails if any file outside modules/ so much as mentions a module type string. Nine modules exist and there is not one switch on module type outside the folder. A rewrite would have to reinvent this and probably would not.

One error contract for the whole API. lib/http/errors.ts maps 13 codes to statuses in one table and fixes the 'never leak a 500's message' rule in one place (errors.ts:63); lib/http/handler.ts is 53 lines. 56 of 60 routes go through route(); the 4 that do not (health, og, poster/frame, client-error) do not return JSON at all. That is the kind of consistency that makes a route review a 30-second job.

app/ is right-sized. 106 files, 8,270 lines, largest file 357 (app/page.tsx), largest API route 215 (app/api/claim/route.ts), most routes under 150. There are no god-routes and no business logic living in pages. The size problem in this codebase is confined to four component files and two driver files.

tests/unit/supabase-mapping.test.ts is a genuinely mature piece of engineering: a 50-line test written in the exact shape that would have caught a specific production incident (size_bytes silently unmapped, the 20 GB storage cap never firing), with the incident written into the file header as the rationale. Most teams write the fix and not the test that generalises it.

Type discipline is real. tsconfig.json turns on strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitOverride and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch. Across ~35,000 source lines there is exactly one `as unknown as` (modules/registry.ts:39, justified), zero @ts-ignore, zero @ts-expect-error, and exactly one file-level eslint disable (lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:41, scoped to the untyped PostgREST row boundary and argued in the comment).

The test suite is honest and fast: 659 tests across 62 files pass in 6.6s, `pnpm lint` is clean, and every one of the 56 'skipped' E2E tests is a conditional project guard (test.skip(({ isMobile }) => ...)) rather than a disabled failure. Nothing is hidden behind .skip or .fixme. The pure-logic core is genuinely well covered: lib/schema.ts, lib/i18n.ts, lib/tenant.ts, lib/entitlements.ts and lib/catalogue-cache.ts are all 100%.

The comments, where they matter, record the rejected alternative rather than restating the code — lib/entitlements.ts:16-28 on why the count caps were removed, lib/tenant.ts:4-20 on the two tenancy modes, modules/contract.ts:30-39 on why meta.shape exists. Every one of the ~50 N-/D- ticket ids and all 16 'doc NN' references I spot-checked resolve to a real file. That is better upkeep than most one-author codebases manage.

Repo hygiene is clean: nothing generated is tracked (no coverage/, .next/, reports/, test-results/), .gitignore is accurate and annotated, knip runs inside `pnpm verify`, and there is a contrast gate (pnpm check:contrast) and a bundle-size gate (pnpm check:bundle) as real scripts rather than aspirations.
themes/ is 382 lines across 4 files with a token contract, a CSS generator shared by guest and preview, and a contrast test — the one part of the styling story that could have sprawled and did not.

findings.title: The Supabase driver is never executed by any test, and has already drifted from the memory driver — unpublished photographs are served to guests in production
findings.evidence: lib/db/memory-repository.ts:742-760 gates listTitles({publishedOnly}) on `t.status === 'ready' && t.liveAt !== null`, with a 12-line comment explaining that gating on `published` 'was the first attempt and it broke withdrawal'. lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1390-1396 does exactly that rejected thing: `.eq('published', true).eq('status','ready')`, with no liveAt check. Worse, lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1625 declares `listPhotosForCatalogue(catalogueId: string)` — it does not accept the `options` parameter the interface declares at lib/db/repository.ts:343, so the `{ liveOnly: true }` passed by the guest-page bundle builder at lib/catalogue-cache.ts:65 is silently dropped in production. TypeScript cannot catch this: a method taking fewer parameters is assignable to one taking more. app/api/admin/uploads/route.ts:107 creates every photo with `liveAt: null`, and supabase/migrations/0012_content_waits_for_publish.sql:11 adds the column with no default, so photographs that no Publish has carried live are on the live guest page today. Nothing tests this: playwright.config.ts:21 sets DATA_DRIVER: 'memory' and every unit test constructs MemoryRepository directly, so all 659 unit tests and all 212 E2E tests run against the driver that is not in production. The only automated contact with SupabaseRepository is the 50-line column-map test and the opt-in tests/integration/drivers.test.ts (~6 Supabase tests, skipped unless RUN_INTEGRATION=1 and credentials are present).
findings.why_it_matters: A photograph a studio uploaded but deliberately has not published appearing on the couple's live wedding page is a phone call, a refund, and possibly a wedding photograph in front of the wrong audience. The N-57 feature — 'content waits for Publish' — is fully implemented in the driver nobody ships and half-implemented in the one they do, while the console confidently tells the operator '3 films will go live when you publish'. Structurally, the 1,869-line file that is production is the least-verified file in the repository.
findings.fix: Two things, in order. (1) Fix the divergence now: add `.not('live_at','is',null)` to the publishedOnly branch of lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1390, and give listPhotosForCatalogue at line 1625 the `options?: { liveOnly?: boolean }` parameter with `.not('live_at','is',null)` when set. (2) Stop it recurring: create tests/contract/repository.ts exporting a describe-block parameterised over a `() => Repository` factory, move the predicate-bearing assertions out of tests/unit/content-publishing.test.ts, credits.test.ts, couple-catalogues.test.ts and transfer.test.ts into it, and run it against MemoryRepository always and SupabaseRepository under RUN_INTEGRATION=1. Start with the ~15 methods whose body contains a predicate or an ORDER BY: listTitles, listPhotosForCatalogue, publishCatalogueContent, countPendingContent, consumeCredit, getCatalogueForSupport, listCataloguesForCouple, listStalledTitles, catalogueCounts, listLikes.
findings.effort: 2 hours for the two bug fixes; 2-3 days for the shared contract suite and porting the existing assertions into it.

findings.title: Only 2 of ~20 Supabase field-to-column maps are held to their schema; the most-edited entity's map is a private inline object with no test, and one doc comment claims a test that does not exist
findings.evidence: lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:67 (TITLE_COLUMNS) and :97 (PHOTO_COLUMNS) are exported specifically so tests/unit/supabase-mapping.test.ts:26-32 can hold them to titleSchema and photoSchema. NOTIFICATION_COLUMNS at line 111 carries the comment '`Notification` field to column, held to the schema by tests/unit/supabase-mapping.test.ts' — but that test file imports only PHOTO_COLUMNS and TITLE_COLUMNS (line 2) and asserts nothing about notifications. Meanwhile the catalogue, the single most-edited entity in the product (35 fields, lib/schema.ts:503-602, including branding, draftBranding, draftModules, premiereAt, passcodeVersion, servedAt, supportAccessUntil), is mapped by a private inline object literal at lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:239-275 that nothing can reach or test, and read back by a separate hand-written mapper at :192-237. toTitle at :285 is likewise hand-written, so adding a field to titleSchema fails the column test (write path) but silently returns undefined on the read path. Orgs, presets, domains, transfers, credits, entitlements, operators and job runs have no map test at all. The file's own header comment at :52-65 describes exactly what this costs: size_bytes was unmapped for the life of migration 0007, every catalogue reported 0 GB, and the 20 GB storage cap never once refused an upload.
findings.why_it_matters: This is not a hypothetical class of bug — it already happened once and the financial exposure was described by the author as 'a partner on a 20 GB plan could have uploaded two hundred'. The team fixed the instance and generalised the fix across 10% of the surface. A silently dropped column on the catalogue row is the scariest version: a draftBranding or passcodeVersion that never writes means a passcode change that does not sign anyone out, or a branding draft that publishes to guests the moment it is typed. And the comment at line 111 is actively misleading — it tells the next reader that a guard exists where none does.
findings.fix: In lib/db/supabase-repository.ts, export the catalogue map (lift the object literal out of fromCatalogue at :239 into a top-level `export const CATALOGUE_COLUMNS`) and do the same for org, preset, domain, transfer, credit and operator, replacing each hand-written `fromX` with `SupabaseRepository.project(x, X_COLUMNS)` (the helper already exists at :320). Then generalise tests/unit/supabase-mapping.test.ts into a table-driven test over `[[catalogueSchema, CATALOGUE_COLUMNS], [orgSchema, ORG_COLUMNS], ...]`, and add the reverse assertion for readers: for each entity, round-trip a schema-parsed fixture through fromX then toX and assert deep equality, which catches the read-side gap the column test cannot. Fix the false comment at line 111 in the same commit.

findings.title: `pnpm lint` does not lint middleware.ts, modules/ or themes/ — `pnpm verify` is greener than the codebase, and the first rule in CLAUDE.md's enforced table is currently broken in four places
findings.evidence: `pnpm lint` (package.json:12, `next lint`) prints 'No ESLint warnings or errors'. Running eslint directly — `npx eslint middleware.ts modules themes` — prints 4 errors, all `no-restricted-properties` on `process.env`, at middleware.ts:23, :34 and :74 (twice). `next lint` with no arguments lints only app/, components/, lib/, pages/ and src/, so middleware.ts, modules/, themes/, scripts/ and e2e/ are never seen. .eslintrc.json:27 lists the intended exemptions (lib/env.ts, lib/log.ts, configs, scripts, e2e, tests) and middleware.ts is deliberately not among them — the exemption it relies on is an accident of tool scope, not a decision. The reads themselves are justified and documented (middleware.ts:32-33: lib/env.ts is server-only and cannot be imported into edge middleware), so the code is fine; the enforcement is not. The lint run also warns that `next lint` is deprecated and removed in Next.js 16.
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md opens its 'working rules, enforced rather than remembered' table with 'process.env only in lib/env.ts — enforced by eslint no-restricted-properties'. That claim is false today, and the two mechanisms that police this codebase have a shared blind spot: the registry test at tests/unit/registry.test.ts:152-154 also walks only app/, components/ and lib/. Two of the nine folders that hold source are outside both nets. Concretely: the day someone runs the codemod the deprecation warning recommends, or upgrades to Next 16, `pnpm verify` goes from clean to 4 errors with no code change — which reads as 'the upgrade broke it' and costs an afternoon of the wrong investigation.
findings.fix: Replace the `lint` script in package.json with an explicit ESLint CLI invocation — `eslint . --ext .ts,.tsx` — with .eslintrc.json's ignorePatterns already covering node_modules/.next/coverage/docs/playwright-report. Add `middleware.ts` to the no-restricted-properties override block at .eslintrc.json:27 with a one-line comment pointing at middleware.ts:32-33, so the exemption is a decision on the record. Extend the walk() roots at tests/unit/registry.test.ts:152-154 to include 'modules' is not wanted (it is the home of the types) but 'themes' and the repo-root .ts files are.
findings.effort: 2-3 hours, including fixing whatever the widened lint surfaces in scripts/ and e2e/.

findings.title: 13,326 lines of UI at 17% line coverage — the four biggest components, including the customizer and the create wizard, have no component test at all
findings.evidence: coverage/coverage-summary.json aggregates to 37.4% overall lines; components/admin is 602/3,564 (17%), components/chrome is 0/110 (0%), components/streaming is 587/1,680 (35%), and the module Guest components sit at 19-27% each (modules/timeline 40/215, modules/checklist 34/182, modules/letter 28/127). There are 7 component test files totalling 801 lines against 75 components totalling 13,326 lines. CreateWizard.tsx (1,006 lines), CustomizerShell.tsx (765), ThemeStudio.tsx (613), PreviewPane.tsx (472), PhotoManager.tsx, SectionInspector.tsx, WatchScreen.tsx and ModuleRenderer.tsx have none. Playwright does carry real weight here — e2e/operator.spec.ts has 16 tests against the customizer and e2e/admin.spec.ts 14 against the console — but every admin spec opens with test.skip(({ isMobile }) => Boolean(isMobile)) (e2e/admin.spec.ts:12, operator.spec.ts:11, upload.spec.ts:23, publish-state.spec.ts:16, credits.spec.ts:13, domains.spec.ts:12, locale.spec.ts:12), so the console has zero automated coverage at phone width beyond the two smoke checks in e2e/responsive.spec.ts.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the inverse of where the risk is. The pure logic — schema, i18n, tenant, entitlements, access — is at 92-100% and is the code least likely to break. The 13k lines of stateful React holding the product's entire differentiator are at 17%, and E2E is a 60-second feedback loop that only runs against the happy path. The practical cost is that every change to CustomizerShell or CreateWizard is verified by a human clicking, which is exactly the tax that makes a codebase feel unmaintainable and makes a rewrite look attractive. CLAUDE.md's own definition of done is a live customizer demo in front of a planner.
findings.fix: Do not chase a coverage number. Add component tests for the four state machines whose bugs are invisible until someone looks: (1) CustomizerShell's commit/undo/redo/autosave path (components/admin/CustomizerShell.tsx:107-120 is the single choke point — drive it directly and assert the undo stack depth of 20, that redo clears on a new edit, and that autosave debounces); (2) CreateWizard's localStorage draft restore and slug derivation (components/admin/CreateWizard.tsx:138-168); (3) UploadManager's retry/resume state transitions, which already has a test at tests/component/upload-manager.test.tsx — extend it to the interrupted path; (4) ModuleRenderer against a stale module type. Then drop the isMobile skip from one admin spec (publish-state.spec.ts is the cheapest) so at least one console flow is exercised at 375px.
findings.effort: 3-4 days for the four suites; half a day for the mobile spec.

findings.title: CreateWizard is 1,006 lines with 29 useState hooks and a 70-line create() that performs two sequenced network calls with inline response casts
findings.evidence: components/admin/CreateWizard.tsx is one exported component spanning lines 55-810, with 29 useState declarations, 4 useEffect blocks, and five steps rendered as sequential `{step === N ? ... : null}` blocks inside a single return. create() at :188-262 posts to /api/admin/catalogues, then conditionally posts to /api/admin/catalogues/{id}/couple, then calls router.refresh(), then advances the step, with four separate inline `as { ... }` response casts (:181, :212, :226, :239) and its error handling spread across three branches. chooseStyle at :122-131 mutates five other pieces of state as a side effect, including `setTemplate(style.templateId as typeof template)` — a cast that exists because the template id's type is inferred from TEMPLATES[0]!.id rather than declared.
findings.why_it_matters: Twenty-nine independent useState calls means the component's legal states are unwritten and unenforced; the localStorage draft restore at :138-153 already only rehydrates five of them, so a refresh at step 3 silently loses occasion, timezone, premiere, privacy and the couple's email. Nothing fails, nothing is logged, and no test covers it. Every future change to the wizard — and the wizard is where a new studio's first half hour goes — starts with reading 1,006 lines to find out which of 29 variables the change touches. This is the single file in the repo where 'I'd rather rewrite it' is a defensible instinct, and it is also the easiest one to fix without rewriting anything else.
findings.fix: In components/admin/CreateWizard.tsx, collapse the 29 useState calls into one useReducer over a `WizardState` type and a discriminated `WizardAction` union — this alone makes chooseStyle (:122) a single dispatch and makes the localStorage mirror at :155-161 serialise the whole state rather than five hand-picked fields. Then move create() (:188) into a `lib/admin/create-catalogue.ts` module that takes the state and returns a result union, so it is testable without mounting React, and replace the four inline casts with zod schemas parsed through a small `postJson(url, body, schema)` helper. Extract each of the five step bodies into its own file under components/admin/wizard/. Target: CreateWizard.tsx under 250 lines.

findings.title: catalogueCounts and the platform console fetch unbounded row sets to compute numbers — the exact cost the Repository interface's own comment set out to avoid
findings.evidence: lib/db/repository.ts:44-54 explains that catalogueCounts exists because the alternative on the list page is 'listTitles per row — a partner with thirty weddings would make sixty round trips to draw one screen, and the page would get slower every wedding they sold'. lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1091-1148 implements it by selecting every title row (`select('catalogue_id, status, published').in('catalogue_id', ids)`), every album row, and then every photo row for the org, and counting them in JavaScript — trading N round trips for one unbounded fetch. Separately, app/admin/platform/couples/page.tsx:21-27 does the thing the comment warns against outright: for each couple org it awaits listOperators and listCataloguesForCouple inside a Promise.all map, i.e. 2 queries per couple, unbounded. The same shape appears at app/admin/platform/studios/page.tsx:26 (creditBalance per studio).
findings.why_it_matters: At today's 6 orgs and 5 catalogues this is invisible. At the documented target of ~10 weddings/month, a studio at 120 catalogues with 300 photographs each pulls ~36,000 rows over the wire to render a list of numbers, and the platform couples page issues ~240 queries per render. Neither page has a limit, an index hint, or a test that would notice. This is the class of problem that presents as 'the console got slow' eighteen months in, by which time the fix is a migration and a rewrite of two pages rather than one SQL function.
findings.fix: Add a Postgres function (a new supabase/migrations file) `catalogue_counts(p_org_id uuid)` returning catalogue_id, titles, ready, published, failed, photos — the repo already uses RPC elsewhere (lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1599, :1807), so the pattern exists — and have lib/db/supabase-repository.ts:1091 call it. For app/admin/platform/couples/page.tsx:21-27, add a single `listOperatorsForOrgs(orgIds)` / `listCataloguesForCouples(orgIds)` pair to the Repository interface and fetch both in two queries. Both MemoryRepository implementations stay trivial loops.
findings.effort: 1 day, including the migration and the memory-driver equivalents.

findings.title: The org-scoping rule is the only rule in CLAUDE.md's enforced table with no automated check — it currently holds perfectly, which is the best moment to pin it
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md lists eight rules as 'lint rules, tests or types, not conventions'; org scoping is not among them, but lib/admin/session.ts:7-13 states the stronger claim that 'a route that does not call one of these functions is visibly unscoped'. Visibly, but not verifiably: I walked every route file under app/api/admin/ and all 49 non-platform routes plus all 11 platform routes do call requireOperator, requireOwnedCatalogue, requireEditableCatalogue or requirePlatformAdmin, and all 10 pages under app/admin/platform/ call getPlatformAdmin followed by notFound(). Nothing in tests/ or scripts/ asserts any of this. By contrast the much lower-stakes module-type rule gets a 35-line filesystem walk at tests/unit/registry.test.ts:123-157.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the boundary where a mistake is a cross-tenant data leak — one studio reading another studio's wedding — which for a wedding product is not a bug report, it is the end of the relationship. The discipline is currently 100%, which means the test costs nothing to add today and will never be this cheap again. It is also the rule most likely to be broken by a hurried route added at 1am, which is how the other 179 commits were written.
findings.fix: Add tests/unit/route-scoping.test.ts in the shape of the existing registry test: readdirSync over app/api/admin/**/route.ts and app/admin/**/page.tsx, read each file, and assert the source contains one of requireOperator|requireOwnedCatalogue|requireEditableCatalogue|requirePlatformAdmin|getPlatformAdmin, with an explicit allowlist array for any deliberate exception (there are none today, so the allowlist starts empty and every future entry is a code-review conversation). Add the rule to CLAUDE.md's table with the test as its enforcement column.

findings.title: The module registry's own helper switches on the string 'billboard' instead of the meta.shape field that exists for exactly this purpose
findings.evidence: modules/registry.ts:93-96: `firstRowInstanceId` returns the first resolved instance where `entry.instance.type !== 'billboard'`. modules/contract.ts:30-39 defines `shape: 'hero' | 'row' | 'grid' | 'prose'` with the comment that it is 'a layout word rather than a module type, for the same reason content is: it lets the wizard describe a shape without a switch on type outside this folder'. Only billboard declares shape:'hero' (modules/billboard/index.ts:19); the other eight are row, grid or prose. The structural test at tests/unit/registry.test.ts:152-154 walks only app/, components/ and lib/, so a hardcoded type inside modules/ is invisible to it.
findings.why_it_matters: The value this function computes decides which posters load eagerly — it is the difference between the guest page hitting the 1.5s-on-4G target in CLAUDE.md's definition of done and missing it. The day a second hero-shaped module is added (a full-bleed photo opener is the obvious one), firstRowInstanceId will name it as the first row and eager-load two cards that are not on screen, silently, with every test still green. It is one line, and it is the only leak in an abstraction that is otherwise held perfectly.
findings.fix: In modules/registry.ts:94, change the predicate to `entry.definition.meta.shape !== 'hero'`. Add an assertion to tests/unit/registry.test.ts that firstRowInstanceId skips every hero-shaped instance, using a second synthetic hero so the test would fail today under the string comparison.

findings.title: Three HTTP header names form the middleware-to-page contract and are defined five times across three files, one of them as a bare string literal
findings.evidence: middleware.ts:16-19 declares const TENANT_HEADER = 'x-mehfilbox-tenant', CATALOGUE_HEADER = 'x-mehfilbox-catalogue' and HOST_HEADER = 'x-mehfilbox-host' locally. lib/address.ts:25 and :27 export TENANT_HEADER and HOST_HEADER with identical values. app/api/og/route.tsx:22 reads `request.headers.get('x-mehfilbox-catalogue')` as a raw literal with no constant anywhere. So the producer and the two consumers each hold their own copy, and nothing connects them.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the wire protocol between the edge middleware and the server components — the mechanism that decides whether a guest arriving on /studio/wedding gets the page or a redirect loop. Typechecking cannot see across the gap, no test asserts the values match, and a rename in middleware.ts would produce a page that silently believes every request is a legacy /c/ arrival and permanently redirects it. lib/address.ts:8-22 spends fifteen lines explaining how load-bearing this handshake is, which makes the duplication more surprising rather than less.
findings.fix: Move the three constants into lib/tenant.ts (already pure, already imported by middleware.ts at line 2, already 100% covered) as TENANT_HEADER, CATALOGUE_HEADER and HOST_HEADER; import them in middleware.ts:16-19, re-export or import in lib/address.ts:25-27, and replace the literal at app/api/og/route.tsx:22.

findings.title: Comment rot has started in the 404-line Repository interface — two JSDoc blocks are attached to the wrong member and one section header has nothing under it
findings.evidence: lib/db/repository.ts:102-103 carries the comment 'Record a platform-admin action. An unaudited platform write is indistinguishable from an intrusion after the fact, so every write path calls this' — but the next declaration, 21 lines later at :116, is publishCatalogueContent. recordPlatformAudit is undocumented at :123. Likewise the block at :104-108 describes countNotificationsSince, which is declared at :121, two members away. The section header '// Platform-authored themes (D-35)' at :128 is immediately followed by '// Custom domains (doc 16 §1)' at :129 with no members between them; the theme methods actually sit at :166-169 under the credits section. Separately, lib/i18n.ts:5 asserts 'Every user-visible string in the product comes from here' while only 2 of 50 admin components import lib/i18n at all — the console is deliberately English-only per docs/reference/00-decision-log.md:541, but the comment does not say so.
findings.why_it_matters: Comments are 15% of source lines here and they are mostly excellent — they record rejected alternatives and real incidents, which is the highest-value kind. That is precisely why drift is expensive: a reader who finds two misattached blocks in the file that defines the persistence contract stops trusting the other 2,300 comment lines in lib/, and then the commentary's whole return on investment is gone. The rot is small and recent — this is the moment to clean it, not after the next 179 commits.
findings.fix: In lib/db/repository.ts, move the block at :102-103 onto recordPlatformAudit (:123) and the block at :104-108 onto countNotificationsSince (:121); delete the orphaned header at :128 or move listCustomThemes/getCustomTheme/saveCustomTheme (:166-169) under it. Amend lib/i18n.ts:5 to say 'every guest-facing string' and cite the English-only console decision. Then split the interface: lib/db/repository.ts is doing the work of six files — move the org/operator/platform members into lib/db/repository.platform.ts, the catalogue/title/photo members into repository.content.ts, and have repository.ts compose them, which is what makes a misfiled comment visible in review.
findings.effort: Half a day including the split.

findings.title: Naming is layered rather than drifting, but two terms are genuinely inconsistent inside the same layer — and one is in a public URL
findings.evidence: The data model says partner (lib/schema.ts:184, orgKindSchema = z.enum(['partner','couple'])) and the UI says studio (533 occurrences across source vs 91 for partner). Mostly that is a deliberate layering and it is fine. Two places are not: the self-registration endpoint is app/api/partners/route.ts while its sibling is app/api/admin/studio/route.ts — same layer, two words for the same actor, and app/api/partners/route.ts:43 falls back to the literal 'studio' when deriving a slug. And couple appears 651 times as the domain term while the codebase also carries client (171) and the coupleOrgId/originOrgId/orgId triple on the catalogue row (lib/schema.ts:504, :521, :572), which takes a paragraph of comment each to keep straight. provider is used consistently as the driver-seam word (video, photos, auth, domains, notify) and tenant consistently as the addressing word — neither is drift.
findings.why_it_matters: Low today: six orgs, one author. The cost is entirely in the future — every new contributor asks 'is a partner a studio?' once, every search for one term misses the other half of the results, and /api/partners is in a URL that a third party could come to depend on. Renaming the enum value costs a migration, so the longer it waits the more it costs; renaming the route costs nothing today because nothing outside components/admin/RegisterForm.tsx calls it.
findings.fix: Rename app/api/partners/route.ts to app/api/studios/route.ts and update the single caller in components/admin/RegisterForm.tsx, keeping a one-line re-export at the old path for a release. Leave orgKindSchema's 'partner' value alone (it is persisted) but add a one-line comment at lib/schema.ts:184 stating that the persisted value is 'partner' and the product word is 'studio', so the next reader stops asking. Decide once whether 'client' is a synonym for 'couple' and delete the loser.
